summary.text: 前 is commonly used for ‘in front,’ ‘forward,’ and ‘before.’ One traditional analysis explains the related graph 歬 as 止 above 舟, depicting a boat moving forward. Another account links 前 to a graph for cutting and its later use for the directional word; the competing histories do not settle which graph came first.

formation.text: One traditional analysis treats 歬 as a semantic compound: 止 above 舟 depicts a boat moving forward. A competing account associates 前 with cutting and proposes that it was later used for the directional word. These accounts disagree about the graph’s history, so 前’s formation remains disputed.

components.text: In the related graph 歬, 止 appears above 舟 in the reported picture of a boat moving forward. This is part of 歬’s analysis, not a proven component of current 前.
In 歬, 舟 represents the boat in the reported picture of forward movement. This analysis belongs to 歬, not the current graph 前.

history.text: 前 is recorded in bronze forms, including one indexed to Western Zhou material, and in small-seal script. These records show forms of the graph but do not date its first lexical use.

Historical accounts disagree about the order: one treats 歬 as the directional graph and 前 as a later way to write its word; another associates 前 with cutting and treats 歬 as the older directional form.

In the cutting account, a graph associated with cutting was reused for the directional word because the words were said to sound alike. This is proposed borrowing between words, not a demonstrated change in meaning. The sound match remains unverified because no independent name and pronunciation for a depicted implement is established; 前’s reconstructed reading alone cannot prove it.
A separate account analyzes 剪 as 刀 plus 歬 serving as a sound element. Historical sources also record cutting-related uses written with 前, but do not establish a sequence leading to the modern forms.

uncertainties.text: The accounts disagree over whether 歬 or a graph involving 刀 came first in the history of directional 前; the sequence remains unresolved.
The cited uses do not securely date the earliest lexical use or establish the order of the motion, spatial, and temporal senses.
The proposed cutting-related borrowing lacks an independently established name and pronunciation for the depicted implement, so the sound match remains unverified.
The bronze and small-seal records support discussion of the graph’s forms, but they do not establish the first lexical use or its earliest meaning.

senses.text: 前 is used for a position in front and for forward direction. The evidence does not securely date the historical emergence of these uses.
前 also means earlier in time or preceding. Its historical development in relation to the spatial sense is not established.

developments.text: Spatial and temporal uses are documented, but their relationship and chronology are not established.

limitations.text: Bronze and seal-form records do not date the first lexical use or establish an earliest meaning for 前. Forward motion is a reported interpretation of 歬, not a proven original sense of 前.
The cutting use may concern a distinct word written with the same graph. The proposed sound-based borrowing is not demonstrated by an independently attested object-name comparison.

overview.text: One account explains 歬 as 止 above 舟, picturing a boat moving forward. A competing account says a cutting graph was reused for the directional word because the words sounded alike; that proposed match remains unverified. 前 commonly means ‘in front’ or ‘before.’

relationships.text: 歬 is identified as a graphic variant of 前. This records their relationship without deciding which form is historically earlier.
